function.name: calculate_mortgage_payment
function.description: Calculate the monthly mortgage payment given the loan amount, annual interest rate, and number of years. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

loan_amount.description: The loan amount. This is a float type value.

annual_rate.description: The annual interest rate in percentage. This is a float type value.

years.description: Number of years the mortgage is amortized over.

message.content: I’m not able to pull up live market data right now. Could you let me know which type of interest rate you’re looking for—e.g., a mortgage rate, a savings account rate, or something else? That way I can give you the most relevant information.
message.reasoning: The user asks "What's the current interest rate". We need to respond with an answer. There's no mention of which type of interest rate (mortgage? savings?). The user might want the current mortgage interest rate. But we don't have real-time data. We can provide typical rates or say we can't fetch real-time data. According to policy, we should not fabricate. So we can say we don't have real-time data but typical rates are X. Or ask clarifying question. Probably best to clarify what kind of interest rate they want. Also we could use the function to calculate mortgage payment if they give us loan amount etc. But they didn't. So just respond asking clarification.
